Imagine breaking your arm and not feeling a single thing.
But it could actually kill you.
Touch a hot pan, and tiny nerve endings in your skin, called nociceptors, spring into action.
Above about forty-three degrees Celsius, their heat sensors switch on and fire an electrical signal.
It races up your arm to your spinal cord, which yanks your hand away before you even feel it.
A split second later, the pain reaches your brain, so you never do that again.
Some people are born unable to feel pain, because of one broken gene.
They chew their tongues, walk on broken bones, and miss deadly infections.
One boy in Pakistan walked on burning coals for crowds, and died at just fourteen after jumping off a roof.
So pain isn't your enemy. It's the alarm that keeps you alive.
